title: Diversity and Inclusion in AI for Recruitment: Lessons from Industry Workshop

bias_targets.methodology: Qualitative evaluation through a co-design workshop using persona-based user stories (e.g., female engineers, genderqueer applicants, mothers returning to work) to identify potential biases in AI candidate matching and job ad summarisation.

Qualitative evaluation using diverse user stories (e.g., ethnic minority professionals) to assess fair representation and identify culturally insensitive language in AI-generated job recruitment tools.
Qualitative evaluation through user stories representing mature-age and older jobseekers to identify age-related biases in dataset representation and AI job suitability matching.

Qualitative evaluation utilizing user stories representing individuals with physical disabilities and neurodivergent conditions (e.g., ADHD) to assess accessibility and reasonable accommodation inclusion in AI job ad summaries.

Qualitative evaluation using user stories for non-native English speakers to identify exclusionary linguistic biases and complex jargon in AI summaries, as well as examining how AI models struggle with gendered languages.
Qualitative evaluation using personas representing recent immigrants and individuals requiring visa sponsorship to uncover potential biases in how AI systems filter and recommend job postings.

Qualitative evaluation through user stories (e.g., individuals with morbid obesity, non-vaccinated status) to explore whether AI highlights necessary physical and health requirements fairly in job summaries.
